sections.instruction: Choose the correct answers (write the correct pronoun in each gap):

questions.prompt: [gap] (We / Us) met Sally yesterday afternoon. [gap] (She / Her) came to the cinema with [gap] (we / us).
questions.explanation: subject: we, she; object after preposition: us

questions.prompt: I phoned Sarah last night and gave [gap] (she / her) the message.
My brother is older than [gap] (I / me), but [gap] (he / him) isn’t as tall as [gap] (I / me) am.
questions.explanation: than me (informal) / than I; subject before verb am

questions.prompt: “Who wants a cup of coffee?” “[gap] (I / Me).”
A: Have you seen Simon today? B: Yes. [gap] (I / Me) saw [gap] (he / him) this morning. [gap] (He / Him) was going to the swimming pool.
A: What did those people want? B: [gap] (They / Them) asked [gap] (I / me) to help [gap] (they / them).

sections.instruction: Complete the sentences using the pronouns in the box:

questions.prompt: Peter and I are going out this evening. [gap]’re going to the cinema. Would you like to come with [gap]?
questions.explanation: Peter and I → we; object → us

questions.prompt: Where are my keys? I put [gap] on the table a moment ago, but now [gap]’ve disappeared.
[gap]’s usually quite cold in New York in the winter.
A: What did you think of the film, Simon? B: [gap] enjoyed [gap] very much.
[gap]’s strange that Kate didn’t come to the meeting.
A: What do the government plan to do about education? B: [gap] say that [gap]’re going to build more schools.
[gap] aren’t allowed to drive a car in Britain until [gap]’re 17 years old.
If you have any problems, just tell someone and [gap]’ll help you.
How far is [gap] from Madrid to Paris?
My sister and I are quite different. [gap]’s much more serious than [gap] am.
questions.explanation: my sister → she; subject before am → I

sections.instruction: Choose the correct answers (write the correct word in each gap):

questions.prompt: We know [gap] (their / theirs) telephone number, but they don’t know [gap] (our / ours).
[gap] (My / Mine) car wasn’t as expensive as [gap] (her / hers).

[gap] (Our / Ours) flat isn’t as big as [gap] (their / theirs), but [gap] (our / ours) is much more comfortable.
